question: “Does G contain a simple path with at least k edges?” is shown NP-complete by:
options: restriction: k = n − 1 is Hamiltonian path
answer: Set k = n − 1 to obtain Hamiltonian path, which proves NP-hardness. Also verify a proposed simple path in polynomial time to establish membership in NP. Both are needed for NP-completeness.
source_answer: A problem with an NP-complete special case is NP-complete.

question: For positive labelled subset-sum items of total W > 0 and target 0 ≤ t ≤ W, which two extra labelled items give the equal-partition reduction?
answer: Add 2W − t and W + t. The new total is 4W, so each half must sum to 2W. The extra items sum to 3W and cannot share a half; the half containing 2W − t therefore needs original items totalling t.

question: Which statement is an established algorithmic guarantee?
options: every unsatisfiable formula is known to have a polynomial-size certificate verifiable in polynomial time
both endpoints of a maximal matching form a vertex cover of size at most twice the optimum
the doubled-MST shortcut tour can have three times the optimum length in a complete metric graph
a polynomial-time algorithm is known for general 3-colourability
answer: A matching uses disjoint edges, so every cover needs at least one endpoint per matched edge. Selecting both gives at most twice optimum; maximality ensures every edge is covered. The doubled-MST guarantee is at most 2, and no general polynomial algorithm for 3-colourability is known. General short certificates for unsatisfiability are also not known.
source_question: Which statement is TRUE?
source_options: “this formula is unsatisfiable” obviously has a short certificate
taking both endpoints of a maximal set of disjoint edges gives a vertex cover at most twice the optimum
under the triangle inequality the MST-walk tour can be three times the optimal TSP tour
source_answer: Any cover needs one endpoint of each chosen edge, so OPT is at least half the cover’s size; (a) is the open co-NP question, (c) is at most twice, (d) is NP-complete.
